s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of respiratory and systemic symptoms following a rapid ascent from a deep-sea dive
salient_findings: Spontaneous echo contrast consistent with microbubbles in the right heart chambers
key_facts: Rapid ascent from a 50 m sea-depth saturation dive
Complaints of dyspnea, lethargy, arthralgia, and mild confusion
Bilateral joint pain worsened by movement without erythema or swelling
Vital signs: blood pressure 90/60 mm Hg, pulse 95 bpm, respiratory rate 24/min, oxygen saturation 90% on room air
Glasgow Coma Scale score of 14
Wells pulmonary embolism score of 3
White-cell count of 13 × 10^9/L
C-reactive protein 73 mg/L
Metabolic acidosis with pH 7.32, PCO2 28 mm Hg, HCO3– 15 mmol/L, and PO2 63 mm Hg
Normal biventricular size and function on transthoracic echocardiography

shortlist.label: Decompression sickness
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid ascent from deep-sea dive, symptoms of dyspnea, lethargy, arthralgia, and mild confusion

shortlist.label: Pulmonary embolism
shortlist.why_kept: Wells pulmonary embolism score of 3, dyspnea, and hypoxia

shortlist.label: Fat embolism syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral joint pain worsened by movement, respiratory distress, and altered mental status

shortlist.label: Air embolism
shortlist.why_kept: Spontaneous echo contrast consistent with microbubbles in the right heart chambers on echocardiography

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and history of rapid ascent from a deep saturation dive are consistent with decompression sickness, which can cause dyspnea, lethargy, arthralgia, and confusion due to the formation of gas bubbles in the bloodstream and tissues.

rejected.label: Pulmonary embolism
rejected.why: The Wells pulmonary embolism score is low and the patient's symptoms and test results do not strongly support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Fat embolism syndrome
rejected.why: There is no mention of a traumatic injury or orthopedic procedure that would increase the risk of fat embolism syndrome

rejected.label: Air embolism
rejected.why: While the patient did have a rapid ascent, the presence of microbubbles in the right heart chambers is more consistent with decompression sickness than air embolism

rejected.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and test results do not meet the full criteria for acute respiratory distress syndrome, and decompression sickness is a more specific and likely diagnosis given the patient's history
